name: VELOCITY FINANCIAL INC

priced.reason: not a repriceable fcff name or no growth supplied

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: The counter to my dismissal is that the cost of equity is not obviously wrong just because it is low, and that even at a defensible 11-13% cost of equity the justified multiple is 1.1-1.3x tangible book against an actual multiple near 1.0x — a real if unspectacular discount — and that the Toorak deal is a genuine re-rating mechanism I am waving away. Buying an origination and asset-management platform while a third party takes the balance-sheet risk converts part of Velocity's earnings from spread income (which deserves a book multiple) into fee and servicing income (which deserves an earnings multiple). If that mix shift is real, the right comparison is not price-to-book at all, and the stock is cheap.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: The purchase price and funding of the Toorak platform, and the disclosed run-rate fee and servicing revenue it carries. If Velocity is paying a modest cash sum for a platform that adds durable capital-light fee income, the counter wins. If it is paying up, or funding it with equity, or if the 'management' arrangement is thin-margin subservicing, it does not. The Q3 or Q4 2026 filings and the closing 8-K will say.
devils_advocate.already_visible: Not yet, and that is the point. The deal was announced four days before this brief and the platform purchase price was not in any source I could reach; the widely repeated '$3.2 billion' figure refers to the portfolio changing hands, not to what Velocity is paying. The market's own reaction is close to nil — the stock is -1.8% over five sessions — which is either the market ignoring it or the market judging it immaterial to Velocity's equity. I cannot tell which.
devils_advocate.unresolved: The purchase price, the funding, and whether Velocity's balance sheet takes any of the Toorak credit. Also unresolved: whether 9.6% NPLs on investor real-estate loans are, as management frames them, low-LTV positions that resolve at or near par, or the leading edge of a credit cycle. I could not read the 10-Q.

what_changed: Two things since the last 10-K. Q2 2026 (reported 2026-08-05): portfolio $7.0B UPB (+19% YoY), NIM 3.66%, core pre-tax ROE 21.8%, diluted BVPS $18.43 (+18% YoY, +3.8% sequentially), adjusted diluted BVPS $20.59, NPLs improved to 9.6%, net income $25.2M. Then, materially, on 2026-08-26 Velocity Commercial Capital signed an Equity Purchase Agreement to acquire the operating platform of Toorak Capital (KKR-backed, ~280 employees, Tampa), disclosed 2026-08-27 in an 8-K under items 1.01/7.01. Reported as an all-cash purchase of the platform, with roughly $3B UPB of Toorak loans being sold to a third-party investment firm that Velocity will then manage, plus forward-flow arrangements to sell future Toorak originations. Toorak's founder-CEO John Beacham stays and becomes an EVP of Velocity Commercial Capital. Expected to close in Q4 2026.
consensus_case: Velocity originates and holds small-balance investor real-estate loans — business-purpose lending to landlords and small commercial owners, a segment banks largely exited. It is a spread book: the portfolio reached $7.0B of UPB in Q2 2026, up 19% year over year, NIM held above target at 3.66%, and core pre-tax ROE was 21.8%. Diluted book value per share compounded 18% year over year to $18.43. At $18.01 the market is paying roughly one times tangible book — which is exactly what the market has always paid for a levered, non-bank, non-prime real-estate lender, no matter how good the reported ROE looks, because the equity is a thin slice under a lot of securitised debt and the loss content of the book is only revealed in a downturn. Non-performing loans at 9.6% are the reason: they are improving, but a book with near-double-digit NPLs does not get a franchise multiple.
key_risks: The headline gap is a discount-rate artifact, not a mispricing — anyone acting on the 97th-percentile cohort rank is acting on a 6.5% cost of equity for a levered non-prime lender
Toorak integration: 280 employees, a founder-CEO retained, and an undisclosed price, closing into Q4 2026
9.6% non-performing loans; investor real-estate credit is the first thing to crack if small-landlord cash flows deteriorate
Securitisation market access is the funding model — a closed ABS window is an existential rather than a cyclical problem
$1.8M average daily dollar volume: a $711M company that cannot be traded in size
watch_for: The Toorak closing 8-K with purchase price, funding source and the acquired platform's revenue
Q3 2026 NPLs — a reversal of the improvement to 9.6% would break the ROTCE assumption
Any equity raise to fund the acquisition, which would change the per-share arithmetic entirely
